newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders expect EU wheat refund near 19.5 Ecus.
newsitem.headline: Traders expect EU wheat refund near 19.5 Ecus.

text.p: European grain traders said on Thursday they expected the European Union to award soft wheat export refunds up to around 19.5 Ecus per tonne at its weekly export tender.
Judging by bids at Thursday's tender, that would release exports of over 400,000 tonnes, which would cover an estimated trade short position of 300,000 tonnes, they said.
"(U.S.) soft red winter has come down to about $150 per tonne so the restitution which goes with that should be 19.50 Ecus per tonne," one senior European trader said.
EU grain tender results are expected around 1600 GMT.
Others put the likely level of refund between 19.25 and 19.50 Ecus per tonne.
Traders said earlier that bids through France for refunds of 19.50 Ecus per tonne accounted for 486,800 tonnes of soft wheat.
French grain office ONIC reported total bids for 662,800 tonnes at refunds between 17.93 Ecus and 21.87 Ecus per tonne.

Traders said that while the refund they deemed most likely would keep pace with U.S. wheat prices, they would still prefer the EU to go further and subsidise the wider gap between European and Argentine prices.
"Argentina is very competitive," said one trader who estimated that a 19.50 Ecu refund would place French wheat close to $150 per tonne, in line with Chicago-based soft red winter.
Others said the EU would need to hike refunds by as much as $20 a tonne or 16 Ecus to compete directly with Argentina, before adjusting for freight differences.
The EU has so far declined to do this, saying it wants to keep away from excessive subsidy spending and avoid confronting the U.S.
